 Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Rekha Palli
 Order
% 21.04.2023
1.
The present appeal preferred by the insurer under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeks to assail the award dated 20.12.2022 passed by the learned MACT.

Vide the impugned award,
the learned Tribunal by taking the functional disability of the injured/respondent no. 1 as 9%,
awarded a compensation of Rs.9,36,439/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
2.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the present appeal is premised on two grounds,
the first being that since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding any licence for driving a heavy vehicle, recovery rights in favour of the appellant ought to have been granted by the learned Tribunal.

He next submits that when the physical disability in one of the legs of the injured itself was found to be 9%, the learned Tribunal could not have treated functional disability with respect to the whole body as 9% but ought to have treated the same as 50% of the physical disability i.e. 4.5%.
3. Having considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the appellant, even though, I am inclined to issue notice on the question of grant of recovery rights in favour of the appellant, I find absolutely no merit in the appellant's plea that since the physical disability in one of his legs was 9%,
functional disability of the injured ought to have been treated as 4.5%.
It is settled law that functional disability is to be determined by the learned Tribunal on the basis of all facts and circumstances.
There can be no uniform proposition that the same must be always 50% of the physical disability of a part of the body, as is sought to be urged by the appellant.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant has not been able to point out any reason as to why the learned National Insurance Company Limited vs Mahendra Singh & Ors on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36527752/

sentences.text: Tribunal's decision of treating the functional disability of the injured as 9% can be said to be otherwise erroneous.
Consequently, this plea of the appellant is rejected.
5. Accordingly, upon the appellant taking steps, issue notice in the appeal confined to the aspect of grant of recovery rights in favour of the appellant.
Taking into account that notice is being issued limited to this aspect, no notice is required to be issued to the respondent no. 1, the claimant.
Notice will, therefore, be issued only to respondent nos. 2 & 3 through all permissible modes.
In the meanwhile, the TCR be requisitioned and digitized before the next date.
CM APPL. 11351/2023 -Stay.
8. This is an application filed by the appellant seeking stay of the impugned award.
Once, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the compensation granted to the claimant, no case is made out for staying the impugned award.
9. The application is, accordingly, dismissed.
Needless to say, in case the appellant succeeds in the present appeal, it will be open for the appellant to seek recovery of the amount paid to the claimant from respondent nos. 2 & 3, as per law.
10.The application stands disposed of.

REKHA PALLI, J APRIL 21, 2023 acm National Insurance Company Limited vs Mahendra Singh & Ors on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36527752/
